title: Galaxy 15 Satellite Anomaly — April 2010
description: On 2010-04-05T09:48:00Z, Galaxy 15 became unresponsive to ground commands. The anomaly occurred during disturbed geomagnetic and energetic-particle conditions. The spacecraft continued transmitting and remained otherwise operational. The role of the space environment in producing the anomaly is an open investigation question.
causal_attribution: Causal attribution is not established by the available evidence.

anchor_event.label: galaxy15_anomaly
anchor_event.description: Last successful ground command contact lost. Satellite entered 'zombiesat' state — transponders active, attitude control nominal, command uplink unresponsive.

recovery_event.label: autonomous_recovery
recovery_event.description: Galaxy 15 autonomously resumed responding to ground commands. Duration of the anomaly is derived from anchor_event and recovery_event timestamps.

data_sources.description: GOES-11 Energetic Particle Sensor — 5-minute averaged electron and proton flux
GOES-11 Magnetometer — 1-minute averaged magnetic field in GSM coordinates
GOES-11 Orbit Ephemeris from SSC — 3-minute position in GSM coordinates

scientific_limitations: GOES-11 was at GEO longitude -135.0° W, approximately 2° from Galaxy 15 at -133.0° W. Particle and field measurements are a proxy, not a direct in-situ sample at the satellite bus.
The 5-minute averaging of EP8 particle flux data smooths sub-minute impulsive flux increases that may have caused single-event upsets.
B_GSM is the local field at GOES-11 orbit, not at the Galaxy 15 spacecraft body. No magnetometer was onboard Galaxy 15.
Causation between the space weather environment and the command anomaly is inferred, not established. Ground software and RF link conditions are not captured in this dataset.
CDAWeb fill values (-1.0E31) indicate data gaps in the Level-2 archive and are removed from the evidence CSV.
GOES-11 ephemeris from SSC is reconstructed orbit data and may differ by tens of kilometres from the real-time position.
